summary.intent: Investigate and fix someguy IPNS routing failures on staging (PR #322 had reverted to delegated-ipfs.dev), then restore someguy as the self-hosted IPNS sidecar with a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback and Prometheus metrics. Followed by fixing a long-standing release-please tagging deadlock.
summary.outcome: Someguy fixed with corrected Docker config (libp2p port, DHT mode, resources) and deployed to staging. API-level fallback to delegated-ipfs.dev added with Prometheus counters. Release-please deadlock root-caused and fixed by changing staging tag format. v0.26.2 released successfully to staging. A final someguy crash on staging (SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY parsing) was discovered and partially fixed but not yet merged.

repo: Someguy staging deployment failed due to three config issues: libp2p port 4004 not exposed (DHT couldn't receive inbound), standard DHT mode instead of accelerated, and too-tight resources (0.5 CPU / 768MB RAM / 512MB libp2p memory).
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY and SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_FD env vars require raw numeric values (bytes/count), not human-readable strings like '1GB'. The staging container was crash-looping because of this.

The DB-first resolve architecture in ipns.service.ts is intentional: DB is always written synchronously before DHT publish, so DB always wins on sequence number comparison. 100% of resolves hit the DB by design.

release-please deadlock ('There are untagged, merged release PRs outstanding — aborting') was caused by staging tags in v*-staging* format matching the root package tag pattern, causing release-please to scan staging pre-releases and mark path '.' as already processed, skipping the real v0.26.x release.
packages/crypto existed at v0.25.1 but was missing from both release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json, causing it to never be independently versioned.
Vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env — env vars must be passed explicitly (e.g., VAR=value pnpm test) or configured in vitest.config.ts.
The throttler bypass uses an x-throttle-bypass header and THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET env var, not NODE_ENV=test. Tests that hit rate limits need this header configured.

Docker healthchecks with CMD-SHELL run inside the container, not on the host — the someguy image has curl but not wget, so wget-based healthchecks would silently fail in CI/staging even if they appeared to work locally when the host had wget.

code.finding: resolveRecord() tries delegated routing (someguy) first then always queries the DB. When both exist, it prefers whichever has the higher sequence number — DB always wins because it's written synchronously while DHT propagation takes 10-30s. Network resolve acts as a cross-check, not a primary source.
backend parameter typed as 'primary' | 'fallback' (not string) for Prometheus label type safety. Fallback to DELEGATED_ROUTING_FALLBACK_URL only triggers after primary exhausts all retries.
Someguy healthcheck must use curl -sf, not wget. Someguy image ships curl but not wget.
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY must be raw bytes (1073741824) not a human-readable string (1GB) — the flag parser is uint64 and rejects the suffix.
Staging tag trigger pattern changed from 'v*-staging*' to 'staging-v*' to prevent collision with release-please's root package tag discovery.

workflow: release-please requires a valid GitHub Release anchor for each tracked path. Manually created releases need the autorelease:tagged label on the release PR and the corresponding git tag — otherwise the next run sees 'untagged merged release PRs' and aborts.
When release-please has no anchor release for a path, it walks the entire commit history (656+ commits in this case), making runs very slow and prone to the Merge plugin deadlock.
Staging tags must not start with 'v' if release-please tracks a root package with the default vX.Y.Z tag pattern. Any v*-staging* tag gets scanned and can shadow the real release.
release-please 'Failed to add label' after PR creation is a transient GitHub API race condition — the PR node isn't yet resolvable in the graph. Manually adding autorelease:pending resolves it.
deploy-staging workflow triggers on tag push directly, independent of tag-staging-release workflow — pushing a staging tag manually will fire the deploy without E2E validation.

friction: Release-please has had recurring tagging failures since the major refactor and reconfiguration — multiple previous fix attempts (PRs #300, #307, #311, #312, #313, #317, #322) all failed to resolve the root cause.
The staging tag format collision with release-please took significant log analysis (400+ lines) to root-cause — the error message 'Missing 1 paths: .' was misleading.
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY crash only discovered after deploying to staging (no Docker on the dev machine to test inside the container locally).
SSH access confusion — the root SSH key for the staging VPS existed but wasn't used initially, leading to a failed SSH attempt with the CI deploy key.
CodeRabbit flagged wget→curl correctly but the human reviewer was uncertain since wget worked locally (due to running on the host, not inside the container).
Throttle bypass required discovering a non-obvious pattern (custom header + secret) rather than a standard NODE_ENV=test guard.
Web E2E failures on main blocked auto-merge of release PR #327, requiring a manual re-run wait loop.
Background task notification for an already-completed commit created unnecessary noise mid-session.
open_items: someguy memory fix (SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY 1GB → 1073741824, SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_FD 100000) needs a PR created and merged — someguy is currently crash-looping on staging.
PR #326 (staging tag format fix) still open and needs merge before the next staging release.
Verify someguy is healthy on staging after memory fix is deployed.
IPNS resolution is 100% DB-first by design — shifting to network-first when sequence numbers match is a future optimization if DB load becomes a concern.
mock-ipns-routing service kept in docker-compose.yml alongside someguy — cleanup deferred (kept for CI isolation).
Load test comparison metrics (someguy vs delegated-ipfs.dev JSON files) were saved locally but not committed — no persistent record in the repo.
packages/crypto now tracked by release-please but its first auto-versioned release will bump from 0.25.1 to whatever release-please calculates from full history — may need monitoring.
